lines.text: Many learners say: My father works in a fabric.
Better: My father works in a factory.
A place that makes things: factory.
Factory! My father works in a factory.

data.wrong: My father works in a fabric.
data.right: My father works in a factory.
data.why: A place that makes things: factory.

native.tip: En español “fábrica”, pero “fabric” en inglés es tela: el edificio es “factory.”
native.caption: 🙈 Error común: “My father works in a fabric.” Falso amigo: “fábrica” es “factory”: “My father works in a factory.” ¡Escucha a Ama y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “factory”. “Fabric” es una tela. El lugar donde se fabrica algo es “factory”. Escribe una frase tuya con “factory” o dila en voz alta: {link}

en.tip: “Fábrica” looks like “fabric”, but “fabric” is cloth. The building is a “factory.”
en.caption: Common mistake: “My father works in a fabric.” False friend: “fábrica” is “factory”: “My father works in a factory.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
